terms.comment: Of children, plants, animals and anything that grows of itself; crēvit, it has grown. With an adjective, English “grow” is “become”: senēscō, grow old (Traupman 77); jam advesperāscit, it’s growing dark (Ter. And. 581).

terms.gloss: grow up, grow to full size
terms.comment: Of growing up to full size: children, young animals, crops.

phrases.latin: Puer autem crēscēbat, et cōnfortābātur plēnus sapientiā
phrases.english: And the child grew, and grew strong, filled with wisdom

phrases.latin: puerōs inpūbēs compertum est, sī plūrimō cibō nimiōque somnō ūterentur, … corporaque eōrum inprōcēra fierī minusque adolēscere
phrases.english: it has been found that if young boys eat too much and sleep too long, … their bodies stay short and grow less
you will say in wonder: ‘where, I ask you, did this grow?’
